Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- 1) Schedule comprehensive in-person examination and initiate broad laboratory evaluation to assess fatigue, mood symptoms, sleep disturbance, and physical contributors; arrange GP visit within the next few days and discuss results with patient.
- 2) Include thyroid function assessment (TSH, free T4) as part of the labs to evaluate adequacy of levothyroxine therapy and potential undertreatment/fluctuating control.
- 3) Obtain complete blood count and iron studies (and basic metabolic panel as indicated) to evaluate for anemia or nutritional deficiencies contributing to fatigue and dyspnea on exertion; correlate with exercise intolerance.
- 4) Safety: continue to monitor mood and suicidality; patient denies current suicidal ideation; document and reassess as part of follow-up.
- 5) Plan follow-up: return visit after initial evaluation to review results, refine differential, and determine next steps (treatment options, referrals if needed).

Subjective:
- Chief complaints: Several weeks of fatigue, low energy, and difficulty waking; poor appetite; reduced ability to perform usual activities.
- Onset and duration: Symptoms began about 6 weeks to 2 months ago; ongoing.
- Sleep: Trouble sleeping; not sleeping well rather than waking early.
- Mood and cognition: Difficulty focusing and staying distracted; mood described as slightly lower; decreased interest in usual activities; decreased libido.
- Other symptoms: Shortness of breath with exertion during sports for the past few months; fatigue impacting activity tolerance.
- Past medical history: Hypothyroidism; on levothyroxine (dose/frequency not documented).
- Medications: Levothyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: None reported.
- Social history: Married, lives with spouse; recently started a new job (~2 months ago).
- Family history: Father died by suicide ~15 years ago; no other psychiatric or medical conditions noted.
- Review of systems: No vision changes; no reported chest pain; no self-harm thoughts reported; no other acute crises described.
- Mental health safety: Denies suicidal ideation or plans.

Objective:
- No vital signs or physical examination findings documented in the transcript.

- In-person examination and labs are planned.

Assessment & Plan:
1) Major depressive disorder (provisional) with somatic and cognitive symptoms
- Assessment: Major depressive symptoms suspected given >6 weeks of low mood, fatigue, reduced energy, anhedonia (decreased interest), poor concentration, and sleep disturbance; onset aligned with a psychosocial stressor (new job). No current suicidal ideation.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript/DDx): 
  - Hypothyroidism (undertreated or fluctuating thyroid function) — consistent with PMH.
  - Insomnia/adjustment-related sleep disorder.
  - Iron-deficiency anemia or other nutritional deficiencies contributing to fatigue.
- Investigations planned: blood tests to evaluate thyroid function (TSH, free T4), CBC, iron studies, and basic metabolic panel as indicated.
- Treatment planned: no pharmacologic therapy started today; management to be discussed with GP after evaluation; consideration of psychotherapy or pharmacotherapy if indicated after results.
- Referrals: arrange GP in-person visit for examination and labs; possible mental health referral if indicated after assessment.

2) Hypothyroidism (undertreated or fluctuating thyroid function)
- Assessment: Consistent with history of hypothyroidism on levothyroxine; fatigue, cognitive slowing, and mood changes could reflect inadequate control.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript/DDx): Major depressive disorder; adjustment insomnia; anemia.
- Investigations planned: TSH and free T4 measurement; CBC; iron studies.
- Treatment planned: review and potential adjustment of thyroid therapy based on lab results; no dose changes documented today.
- Referrals: not specified; to be addressed via the GP visit.

3) Iron-deficiency anemia or nutritional deficiency contributing to fatigue and exertional dyspnea
- Assessment: Fatigue and exertional dyspnea raise concern for anemia or nutritional deficiency, though no lab data yet.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx): Iron-deficiency anemia; other nutritional deficiencies.
- Investigations planned: CBC with differential, iron studies (serum ferritin, iron, TIBC), and repeat if indicated after initial results.
- Treatment planned: dependent on results; start appropriate management after labs.
- Referrals: none specified; to be guided by PCP after results.
